title: Bigger flowers with more variety (updated)
question: Which bed has the flowers you asked for, at a plant count you would accept?
context_md:
Supersedes card 20260911T051258362Z-83eaba (a two-way A/B) -- the coordinator's follow-up asked for the size that actually holds the played bed's population, not just the biggest-looking head. Three panes, same frame (6,000), same seed (1): **A** is `main` (organ_cluster 9, fixed, no variety, two petal bands). **B** is what shipped this PR (organ_cluster 12, +33%, per-individual spread 0.3x-1.7x, three petal bands). **C** is 16 (+78%), tried first and not shipped.

**The term found**: every organ cell pays `MAINTENANCE_PER_CELL` like any other living tissue, continuously, for as long as it stands -- measured in isolation (a hand-placed head, one `organism_upkeep` tick) as an exact `MAINTENANCE_PER_CELL x extra-cells` delta, not a guess. That charge is separate from and untouched by the `Ripen`-cost re-derivation (which only reaches the one-off flower-set/fruit-ripen charges).

**Honest finding, not fully resolved**: none of 9, 12 or 16 reliably holds plant count within -25% of `main` on all three seeds -- `labforage scenario=played_bed frames=120000`: main 464/574/303; size 16: 322/170/259; size 12: 356/93/158; size 9 (variety+colour only, no size change): 348/299/248. Seed 2 is the outlier at every size and gets *worse* from 16 to 12 before partly recovering at 9 -- not the clean relationship the maintenance term alone predicts, which points at the slot-9 size *variance* itself as a second live effect, untested for want of time. 12 ships as the middle ground with the open question on record.
